title: fix: read developer earnings from materialized events
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
\`developer_earnings_today\` (behind \`/balance/today\`) scanned a full week of \`generation_event_v2\` on every call because the developer columns aren't in its sort key: 16.5M rows per call, ~77B rows and ~1,370 vCPU-seconds a day in prod.

- Reads \`activity_earnings_events\` instead, which the existing BYOP and community-reward MVs already fill and which is sorted by \`dev_user_id, timestamp\` (same table the Activity earnings chart uses)
- Keeps the old \`markup_rate > 0\` condition for BYOP rows via \`reward_rate\`, so results don't change
- No schema change or backfill; endpoint name, params and response shape are unchanged

Checked against prod data: identical \`paid_week\`/\`tier_week\` for all 48 developers with earnings in the last 7 days (167.5246 Pollen total both ways). Largest developer: 16.5M → 33k rows read, 0.36 s → 0.008 s.

\`deployment create --check\` passes on staging. Tinybird still needs a manual deploy (staging, then prod) after merge.

gist.headline: A shorter path to Pollen
gist.blurb: The earnings lookup takes the garden path in the good sense: fewer rows to wander through, same Pollen totals at the end.
gist.summary: The /balance/today developer earnings query reads materialized activity_earnings_events instead of scanning generation_event_v2, cutting the largest developer lookup from 16.5M to 33k rows while preserving paid_week, tier_week, and the response shape.
gist.impact: Developer earnings lookups retain the same totals and API response; in the production-data check, the largest lookup fell from 0.36 to 0.008 seconds.
gist.visual_concept: Depict developer earnings as Pollen gathered from a small, neatly tended row of event flowers rather than an enormous field of raw records. Polli, wearing a tiny accountant's visor, follows the shorter path to a retro balance terminal; a CRT robot checks that the totals match.
